messages:
marco: Heads up — production LCP jumped on dashboard after the vizlib bump. Happening across multiple dashboards, not just heatmap. noticed around 03:20 UTC. :grimacing:
natalie: saw the same in Sentry. stack traces point to `vizlib/dist/index.js` big parse time and a bunch of polyfills included. bundle report indicates the new release undid tree-shaking for `geo-utils` and pulled in `date-fns/locale/*`.
ryan: is this the change that switched from ESM imports to a cjs fallback for older browsers? PR #482 did that fallback to avoid breakage.
sylvia: yes. the webpack rule now forces `main` field resolve for vizlib to keep compatibility. that caused the shipped entrypoint to be the prebuilt UMD which includes internal polyfills.
marco: ugh. so the chart chunk went from 220KB gz to 1.1MB gz for first paint. that alone explains the parse spike.
ops-bot: deploy "web-client@2026.03.21-vizlib-upgrade" completed 2026-03-21T03:18:01Z (canary 15%).
ryan: extra wrinkle: the router's prefetch policy aggressively preloads neighboring dashboard widgets when navigation starts. with the bigger chunk we're now saturating main thread and that delays hydration which triggers retry logic in routing -> more prefetch attempts -> repeated IO. looks like a feedback loop.
natalie: on the quota side, prefetch scheduler will abort requests when concurrentPrefetch > 6 per tab, but because parse blocks, abort handlers aren't running promptly and prefetch tasks queue up server-side. we're hitting backend rate limiting and then falling back to server-rendered placeholders, causing additional telemetry pings.
sylvia: we should be careful; product wanted the vizlib change for improved panning smoothness, but this compatibility fallback regressed bundle shape.
marco: quick mitigation options? rollback the vizlib update, or lazy-split the problematic modules and force a dynamic import for `geo-utils` and `locale` only.
ryan: I can push a canary hotfix that adds an explicit splitpoint:
```js
// force separate chunk
const geo = () => import(/* webpackChunkName: "viz-geo" */ 'vizlib/dist/geo-utils')
```
That should keep the main chart chunk small.
ops-bot: canary scale change requested by ryan: set to 5%.
build-bot: CI passed for hotfix branch.
marco: also reduce prefetch concurrency to 3 temporarily to avoid router thrash. config flag `prefetch.concurrency` is runtime-updateable via feature flags.
natalie: I'll flip the flag and monitor. Lowering to 3 should reduce backend quota pressure.
sylvia: long-term we should update our module resolution rules so packages with modern ESM exports prefer `module`/`browser` fields. patching fallback in webpack was a mistake for this package. create an RFC?
ryan: agreed. follow-ups: 1) hotfix dynamic split + lower prefetch concurrency 2) pause vizlib canary rollout until next build with ESM resolution fix 3) add unit test on CI that validates bundle delta per splitpoint (fail if > 200KB gz).
prod-analytics: running perf job now on staging after hotfix branch deploy; will post LCP and parse time diffs in ~10m.
marco: thanks. small action items: ryan cuts hotfix PR, natalie flips prefetch flag, ops-bot hold canary at 5% while we validate, sylvia writes RFC about resolver rules. postmortem if change went to prod.
ryan: cutting PR now. including a smoke test script:
```
// smoke: load /dashboard/summary and /dashboard/geo in parallel and capture performance.timing
node smoke-load.js --parallel=2 --samples=5
```
sylvia: I'll draft the RFC template and include examples of package.json fields we prefer.
marco: one more note — product asked for the vizlib upgrade timeline; let's keep them in the loop but don't promise immediate re-release. we need to validate the ESM fix first.
prod-analytics: perf job results: parseMain decreased ~620ms after hotfix on staging, LCP returned to baseline for first-view samples. KV-prefetch retry count also dropped ~78%.
marco: perfect. moving forward with canary hold and RFC. thanks team. :raised_hands:
